moments.selftext: Is this all true, @grok? 140–200 Israelis detained March–Sept. 2001 in what reports called potentially the largest spy ring ever found on U.S. soil. Young Israelis posing as “art students” hit federal offices and agents’ homes selling paintings. A leaked DEA memo flagged intel/explosives backgrounds. Many lived in the same Hollywood, FL apartment complexes and neighborhoods as Mohamed Atta and other 9/11 hijackers. Separately, the Lower Manhattan Cultural Council ran an artist residency on the 91st and 92nd floors of the North Tower — immediately below where Flight 11 struck (floors 93–99) — giving international artists 24-hour studio access in unused office space. The 2001 group included artists from multiple countries, among them Israel. On Sept. 11, 2001, five Israelis from Urban Moving Systems were stopped around 4 p.m. in a white van on Route 3 in East Rutherford, NJ. A witness told police they were filming the burning Towers, smiling, hugging, and giving high-fives. An FBI alert said they were “seen celebrating.” Bomb-sniffing dogs alerted on the van; a bomb squad searched it and found no explosives. They were held for months, then deported for visa violations.

moments.selftext: An NBA journeyman who only made $18 million is about to be a billionaire. Omri Casspi already made history when he entered the NBA in 2009. He was the first Israeli player to play in the league, played 10 seasons in the NBA for 7 teams, and won a ring as an in-season member of the Warriors in 2018. But the biggest win of his career came when he retired and founded Swish Ventures. A venture capital firm that started in early 2025 focused on early-stage startups in cybersecurity and AI. Casspi usually invests $20 million per company which is a relatively bigger amount than the average, especially for startup companies. But to him, it's part of the risk of running a business (via Calcalist): “I know $20 million is a large check for the early stages of a company’s life, but I want to find the best opportunities that exist, and in the companies I invest in, I usually put in more money than average. This is a small group of exceptional entrepreneurs.” It's only been less than 2 years, but some of his investments have reaped big rewards. ➡️ Invested in Cognition when it was valued at $150 million (now valued at $26 billion) ➡️ Invested in Upwind Security when it was valued at $65 million (now valued at $3 billion) Swish currently has around 20 companies in its portfolio, with eight reportedly reaching unicorn status, per Globes. Today, Casspi's assets under management are at $800 million High risk, high reward. 💰
